title: Spatial instability of a homogeneous superconductor after an interaction quench
authors: Medha Roy Choudhury, Sankha Subhra Bakshi, Pinaki Majumdar, Amit Ghosal
abstract: We investigate the quantum dynamics of a conventional superconductor, described by the attrac- tive Hubbard model, driven far from equilibrium by quenching the Hubbard attraction. We evolve the full density matrix of the system in time using the Heisenberg equation of motion, tracking the spatiotemporal dynamics of the pairing and density fields. We use very weakly inhomogeneous initial conditions to probe the stability of the homogeneous dynamics to spatial perturbations. At initial times after the quench the pairing and density fields remain homogeneous in space while fluctuating in time. However, depending on the quench strength the spatially uniform dynamics can become unstable beyond a threshold time, with emergence of spatial textures. The onset time for the instability depends on the strength of the quench and the initial inhomogeneity. At long times the system evolves towards a state with significantly reduced spatial heterogeneity. The time dependence of the global superconducting order parameter suggests two broad categories of re- sponse to a quench. One of these involves strongly inhomogeneous pairing and bond currents in the nonequilibrium superconductor.
summary: This work analyzes the non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of a superconductor modeled by the attractive Hubbard model after an interaction quench. The research demonstrates that the initial homogeneous state becomes spatially unstable, leading to the formation of complex textures and coupling between superconducting and charge density wave orders. This highlights the rich, non-equilibrium physics that emerges when quantum systems are driven far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The study investigates the spatial instability of a homogeneous superconductor following a sudden quench of the interaction strength.
main_result: The homogeneous superconducting state becomes unstable beyond a critical quench strength, leading to the emergence of spatial textures and non-equilibrium dynamics characterized by fluctuating currents and potential charge density wave (CDW) formation.
method: The dynamics are simulated by evolving the full density matrix using the Heisenberg equation of motion in real space, tracking various order parameters over time.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a conventional superconductor described by the attractive Hubbard model, subjected to a sudden quench of the interaction parameter U.
key_observables: Spatial Inhomogeneity ($\mathcal{R}(t)$), Global SC Structure Factor ($S_{	ext{SC}}(t)$), RMS Current ($J_{	ext{RMS}}(t)$), and CDW Structure Factor ($S_{	ext{CDW}}(t)$).
important_parameters: Quench strength ($u_r$), initial inhomogeneity ($\mathcal{R}_0$), and time evolution regimes (Regime I and II).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field decoupling for simplified equations, and the study uses phenomenological fitting forms for late-time relaxation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the growth of spatial inhomogeneity ($\mathcal{R}(t)$), the time evolution of SC and CDW orders showing anti-correlated oscillations, and the formation/coarsening of spatial SC textures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the time evolution through different dynamical regimes following the quench, detailing the onset of spatial instability, the interplay between SC and CDW orders, and the long-time non-equilibrium steady state.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed insights into non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated superconducting systems, showing how quench dynamics can drive the system into spatially inhomogeneous states, which is relevant for understanding quench dynamics in quantum materials.
